prompt: Ana's first configuration holds only `data.aws_caller_identity.current` and `data.aws_region.current`, plus two outputs. What does `terraform apply` change in the account?
hint: Read the summary line of the apply.

choices.text: It creates two read-only records that describe the caller
choices.why: A data source creates nothing in the account; its answer is recorded in the state, not in AWS.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right: `0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed`. Data sources only ask; the apply saved the outputs and moved nothing.

choices.text: It tags the account with the region it was read from
choices.why: Reading the region writes nothing; it is a fact about the connection.

choices.text: It creates an IAM user for Terraform to work as
choices.why: The identity already exists: it is whoever the credentials belong to, moto's placeholder user in the lab.

prompt: What address does a configuration use to read the account number from `data "aws_caller_identity" "current" {}`?
hint: Data sources live under their own prefix.

choices.text: `aws_caller_identity.current.account_id`
choices.why: Without the `data.` prefix that is the address of a resource, and no such resource exists.

choices.text: `var.aws_caller_identity.account_id`
choices.why: `var.` is for input variables, which the caller sets; a data source is answered by the provider.

choices.text: `data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id`
choices.why: Yes: `data.TYPE.NAME.attribute`.

choices.text: `data.current.account_id`
choices.why: The type is part of the address; two data sources of different types may share a name.

prompt: A block that asks the provider a question and keeps the answer, creating nothing, starts with the keyword ___.
hint: The other block keyword is `resource`.

prompt: `terraform state list` shows `data.aws_region.current` beside the resources. What does that entry mean?
hint: Is it read again on the next plan?

choices.text: Terraform now owns the region and will destroy it with the rest
choices.why: A destroy never touches a data source; nothing was created.

choices.text: A cached answer from the last read, which the next plan replaces by asking again
choices.why: Right. The state keeps the last answer, and each plan asks again because the thing may have changed.

choices.text: The region is locked so that other configurations cannot read it
choices.why: Reading locks nothing; any number of configurations can read the same thing.

choices.text: An import of the region into this configuration
choices.why: Importing brings a resource under management (lesson 8); a data source is only looked at.

prompt: The network team's VPC already exists. Why is writing a `resource "aws_vpc"` block with the same range the wrong way for Ana to use it?
hint: What does a resource block mean?

choices.text: Terraform would reject a range that another VPC already uses in the account
choices.why: AWS accepts two VPCs with the same range; lesson 1 created exactly that by running a script twice.

choices.text: It would create a second VPC with the same range, beside theirs
choices.why: Yes. A resource block means "make this exist", not "find this".

choices.text: It would take the network team's VPC over and rename it
choices.why: Terraform does not adopt existing resources from a block; that takes an import, lesson 8.

choices.text: A resource block has no `tags` argument
choices.why: Resources carry tags all the time; the problem is what the block asks for.

prompt: In Ana's plan, the security group's `vpc_id` shows a real `vpc-…` id rather than `(known after apply)`. Why?
hint: When was `data.aws_vpc.shop` read?

choices.text: She typed the id into the configuration after looking it up
choices.why: Nothing in `network.tf` names an id; that is the point of the lookup.

choices.text: The security group was created during an earlier apply
choices.why: The plan says it will be created; the id comes from the VPC, not from the group.

choices.text: The VPC lookup was answered during the plan, before anything was created
choices.why: Right. Its query was fully known, so it was answered first, and its id is a plain value in the plan.

choices.text: moto returns ids in advance for any VPC
choices.why: The same happens against real AWS; it is how Terraform orders reads, not a quirk of the lab.

prompt: Ana's configuration reads the VPC and two subnets and creates one security group. How many things does `terraform plan -destroy` say it would destroy?
hint: Only what the configuration created.

prompt: What does Ana's configuration depend on now that it finds the network by tag? Choose all that apply.
hint: Think about what the network team could change.

choices.text: The VPC keeping the tag `Name = shop`
choices.why: Yes; the tag is the query.

choices.text: No other VPC carrying the same tags
choices.why: Yes; a singular lookup refuses two matches, as the last section shows.

choices.text: The VPC keeping the id it had when she wrote the file
choices.why: No; that is what the lookup frees her from. A rebuilt VPC with the same tags is found again.

choices.text: The network team running Terraform
choices.why: No; they used the AWS CLI, and the lookup worked.

choices.text: The public subnets keeping `Tier = public`
choices.why: Yes; `aws_subnets` filters on that tag.

prompt: With several `shop-web-*` images, what does `most_recent = true` make `data "aws_ami"` do?
hint: It is a tie-break.

choices.text: Pick the newest of the images it matched, by creation date
choices.why: Yes, among the images the filters matched.

choices.text: Download the newest image into the configuration directory
choices.why: An AMI is never downloaded; the data source returns its id and attributes.

choices.text: Keep its first choice even after a newer image appears
choices.why: The opposite: it is asked again on every plan, which is the danger the section shows.

choices.text: Ask the image team for a new build before each plan
choices.why: A data source only reads what exists; it triggers nothing.

prompt: Ana changed nothing in her files, yet the plan shows `aws_instance.web must be replaced`. What changed?
hint: Look at the line marked `# forces replacement`.

choices.text: The provider was upgraded and now handles instances differently
choices.why: The provider version is pinned by the lock file; the plan names `ami` as the cause.

choices.text: Someone stopped the instance by hand in the console
choices.why: A stopped instance is not a reason to replace it; the diff is in `ami`.

choices.text: The data source's answer
choices.why: Right. A newer image matched `shop-web-*`, `most_recent` picked it, and `ami` cannot change on a running machine.

choices.text: The subnet ran out of addresses
choices.why: Nothing in the plan points at the subnet; it names the image.

prompt: For production, which change makes an image upgrade a reviewed decision instead of a side effect of the next plan?
hint: The section rewrote `image.tf`.

choices.text: Run `terraform plan` less often
choices.why: The next plan, whenever it comes, still picks up the newest image.

choices.text: Filter on the exact image name, held in a variable
choices.why: Yes. Moving it is now a one-line diff somebody reviews.

choices.text: Add a second `filter` block on the architecture so that fewer images match
choices.why: Every new build has the same architecture, so the newest still wins.

choices.text: Set `owners` to the image team's account instead of `self`
choices.why: That narrows whose images are searched, not which build is chosen.

prompt: A scratch environment runs `most_recent = true` on purpose. Production pins the name. The image team publishes a new build. What does each environment's next plan show?
hint: One follows the newest, one asks for one name.

choices.text: Both show a replacement, because the image list changed
choices.why: The pinned filter still matches only the old name, so its answer did not change.

choices.text: Neither changes until somebody edits a file
choices.why: The scratch one changes with no edit: that is what `most_recent` was chosen for.

choices.text: The first is replaced; the second has nothing to do
choices.why: Right; the same image list gives two answers to two different questions.

choices.text: Production fails because two images now match `shop-web-*`
choices.why: Production no longer filters on the wildcard; it names one build.

prompt: `data "aws_availability_zone" "app"` takes `name = aws_subnet.app.availability_zone`, and the plan shows the name `sa-east-1a` already. Why is it still read during apply?
hint: Read the comment under its heading in the plan.

choices.text: Zone lookups are slow, so Terraform runs them last
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with it; the plan gives the reason in a comment.

choices.text: It refers to the subnet, a resource with changes still pending
choices.why: Yes: "depends on a resource or a module with changes pending". The subnet is created first.

choices.text: The zone name is unknown until AWS assigns one to the subnet
choices.why: The name is written in the subnet block and shown in the plan; it is known.

choices.text: moto cannot answer zone lookups during a plan
choices.why: The same lookup was answered during the next plan, once the subnet existed.

prompt: After the apply that created the `app` subnet, the output `app_subnets` was `tolist([])`. What explains the empty list?
hint: When was the tag lookup read, compared with when the subnet was created?

choices.text: It was read during the plan, before the subnet it looks for existed
choices.why: Right. Nothing referred to the subnet, so nothing made it wait, and an apply carries out the plan it was given.

choices.text: moto indexes tags a few seconds after creation
choices.why: The next plan found the subnet straight away; timing inside moto is not the cause.

choices.text: The subnet got its tags after it was created
choices.why: The plan shows the tags as part of the creation.

choices.text: `aws_subnets` ignores subnets that Terraform itself manages
choices.why: The next plan listed exactly that subnet; the lookup just ran too early.

prompt: Ana adds `depends_on = [aws_subnet.app]` to the tag lookup, then adds an `Owner` tag to the subnet. What does the plan show for `app_subnets`?
hint: The subnet now has a change pending.

choices.text: The same list as before, because the subnet keeps its id
choices.why: The value would be the same after the apply, but the plan cannot know it yet.

choices.text: An empty list again
choices.why: The read is not made early any more; it waits until the apply.

choices.text: `(known after apply)`
choices.why: Yes. Any pending change to a dependency defers the read, and everything built from it becomes unknown.

choices.text: An error, because `depends_on` is refused on data sources
choices.why: It is accepted; the cost is the deferral, not an error.

prompt: In a plan, the symbol that marks a data source to be read is ___.
hint: Two characters, an arrow pointing left.

prompt: What does `data "aws_iam_policy_document"` produce?
hint: Look at the attribute the bucket policy uses.

choices.text: An IAM role that the bucket assumes when it serves objects
choices.why: It creates nothing in IAM; it only writes a document.

choices.text: A JSON policy
choices.why: Yes, in `.json`, computed by the provider from the HCL blocks.

choices.text: A copy of the policy already attached to the bucket in AWS
choices.why: It reads nothing from AWS; it builds a new document from what you write.

choices.text: A report of who accessed the bucket
choices.why: Access logs are a different service; this is a policy.

prompt: Put the steps of the apply that created the shop's bucket policy in the order they happened.
hint: The document needs the bucket's ARN.
trap: Reading the policy document before the bucket is the usual slip: its `resources` need the bucket's ARN, which only exists once AWS has made it.

prompt: `data.local_file.office` was read at the start of the plan, while the policy document waited for the apply. What made the difference?
hint: Compare what each one is given.

choices.text: Local files are read before anything in AWS, as a rule of the local provider
choices.why: Providers have no such priority; the timing comes from what is known.

choices.text: The policy document is slower to compute than reading a file
choices.why: Speed is not a reason Terraform gives; the plan said "config refers to values not yet known".

choices.text: The file's `filename` was known; the bucket's ARN was not
choices.why: Right. A read waits exactly as long as something it is given is unknown.

choices.text: The policy document has `depends_on` set on the bucket
choices.why: It has none; the reference to `aws_s3_bucket.assets.arn` is enough.

prompt: Match each lookup to what the plan did.
hint: Singular data sources want exactly one.

pairs.right: Error: no matching EC2 VPC found

pairs.left: `aws_subnets` tagged `Tier = private`, which no subnet has
pairs.right: An empty list, and no error

prompt: Ana's untouched configuration suddenly fails with `multiple EC2 VPCs matched`. What happened?
hint: Her files did not change.

choices.text: Her state file was corrupted and lists the VPC twice
choices.why: The error comes from the lookup's answer, not from the state.

choices.text: Somebody else created another VPC carrying the same tags
choices.why: Yes: the staging copy carried `Name = shop` too.

choices.text: The network team deleted the production VPC, and the error lists what remains
choices.why: Both VPCs were there; `describe-vpcs` showed prod and staging.

choices.text: moto duplicated the VPC on restart
choices.why: The second VPC has another range and another Environment tag; somebody made it.

prompt: Why is the empty list from `aws_subnets` more dangerous than the error from `aws_vpc`?
hint: Which of the two stops anything?

choices.text: Because the empty list stays in the state and is not refreshed
choices.why: It is read again on every plan like any data source.

choices.text: Because an empty list makes Terraform delete the subnets it cannot see
choices.why: A data source never deletes anything; the danger is what is built on the empty answer.

choices.text: It applies quietly
choices.why: Right. No error and no warning: something built on zero subnets goes through, where the error stopped the plan.

choices.text: Because plural data sources are read once and kept
choices.why: Plural or singular, a data source is read on every plan.

prompt: Which fix did Ana apply when the staging copy broke her VPC lookup?
hint: She asked for what she meant.

choices.text: Added `most_recent = true` to `data "aws_vpc"` so that the newest VPC wins
choices.why: `aws_vpc` has no such argument, and the newest VPC was the staging one anyway.

choices.text: Added `Environment = "prod"` to the tags it filters on
choices.why: Yes; the next plan found one VPC and reported no changes.

choices.text: Copied the production VPC's id into the configuration
choices.why: That works until the network is rebuilt, the problem the lookup was meant to solve.

choices.text: Asked the network team to delete the staging VPC
choices.why: The staging network is legitimate; the query was too loose.

prompt: A colleague says: "Our app reads the network with `data "aws_vpc"`, so if we destroy the app, the VPC goes with it." What is wrong?
hint: Who created the VPC?

choices.text: Nothing; a destroy removes data sources after the resources
choices.why: The plan -destroy listed one thing: the security group. Data sources are never destroyed.

choices.text: A destroy removes what its own configuration created; reading gives no ownership
choices.why: Right; reading the VPC gave no ownership of it.

choices.text: The VPC is destroyed, but only after asking the network team for approval
choices.why: Terraform has no notion of asking another team; it does not destroy what it only read.

choices.text: The VPC is kept, but its subnets are removed with the app
choices.why: The subnets were read too, through `aws_subnets`; they are equally out of reach.

prompt: Which of these make a data source's read wait until the apply? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two reasons appear in the plans of this lesson.

choices.text: An argument that refers to a value not yet known
choices.why: Yes: the policy document waiting for the bucket's ARN.

choices.text: A reference to a resource with changes pending
choices.why: Yes: the zone lookup referring to the new subnet.

choices.text: A `depends_on` on a resource with changes pending
choices.why: Yes: the tag lookup after the `Owner` tag was added.

choices.text: A data source that reads a file on the laptop
choices.why: `local_file` was read at the start of the plan; its filename was known.

choices.text: A filter with a wildcard such as `shop-web-*`
choices.why: The image lookup was read during the plan; a wildcard is a known value.

prompt: Ana's application needs the database team's security group id. That team manages it with its own Terraform configuration. What does the lesson point to as the stronger contract than a tag lookup?
hint: Something the other configuration publishes on purpose.

choices.text: A `data "aws_security_group"` filtered on its name
choices.why: That is still a guess about something nobody promised to keep unique.

choices.text: Its outputs, read with `terraform_remote_state`
choices.why: Yes; outputs are an interface the other team chose, and lesson 8 uses them.

choices.text: A copy of their `.tf` files inside Ana's configuration
choices.why: Copied resource blocks would create a second security group.

choices.text: An `import` of their security group into Ana's state
choices.why: Then two configurations would manage one resource and fight over it.

prompt: Which data source used in this lesson made no request to AWS at all?
hint: It builds its answer from the blocks you write.

choices.text: `aws_subnets`
choices.why: It asks EC2 which subnets match.

choices.text: `aws_caller_identity`
choices.why: It asks STS who the credentials belong to.

choices.text: `aws_ami`
choices.why: It searches EC2's image catalogue.

choices.text: `aws_iam_policy_document`
choices.why: Yes; the provider writes the JSON locally. (`local_file` also stays off AWS, reading the laptop's disk.)
